zones.name: Kharvos Prime
zones.description: A fortified hive world at the heart of the Drift, home to three billion souls under the Astra Militarum's watch. The system's capital, and the first thing anyone attempting to enter the Drift has to get past.

log.text: The warp storm that sealed the Kharvos Drift for three centuries has finally broken. Astra Militarum forces from the Cadian 771st make landfall at Kharvos Prime, reclaiming the hive spires in the Emperor's name and declaring the system open once more.
Vox-traffic from orbit reports unidentified voidcraft massing beyond the system's edge. High Command orders all garrisons to full alert.

zones.name: Vantage Solar
zones.description: A void-station in high geostationary orbit, bristling with augur arrays and long-range weapon batteries. The Adeptus Astartes garrison here answers to no local command.

log.text: A single strike cruiser broke from the Kharvos relief fleet and made for the system's edge without explanation. The Adeptus Astartes rarely explain themselves. Vantage Solar's void-shields flickered to life within the hour — and have not powered down since.

zones.name: The Reliquary
zones.description: An orbital shrine-station consecrated by the Order of the Sacred Rose, now a waypoint for pilgrims drawn to a system long thought lost to the Emperor's light.

log.text: The Order of the Sacred Rose consecrates the orbital shrine-station, declaring it a beacon of the Emperor's light in a system long lost to darkness. Pilgrims begin to arrive even as the void beyond remains unsecured.

zones.name: Aurun's Forge
zones.description: An ash-choked forge world riddled with pre-Imperial ruins. The Adeptus Mechanicus believes STC fragments lie in its deep, unexcavated vaults.

log.text: The Adeptus Mechanicus arrives in force, its tech-priests eager to reclaim the pre-Imperial forge complexes buried beneath Aurun's ash fields. STC fragments are rumored to lie in the deep vaults.

zones.name: Aurun's Slag-Moon
zones.description: A tortured little moon stripped raw by centuries of strip-mining, feeding raw ore straight into Aurun's Forge below. The tech-priests insist the moon 'sings' when the extraction rigs run at full capacity.

log.text: With the Forge reclaimed, servitor crews are dispatched to the adjoining slag-moon to restart the old ore-extraction rigs — silent for three centuries, and reportedly reluctant to start again.

zones.name: Skarn's Maw
zones.description: A crater-pocked moon dominated by the wreck of a crashed hulk. Warboss Skarnag Grimjaw's Bloodmoon Krew has called it home for longer than anyone can prove.

log.text: Warboss Skarnag Grimjaw and his Bloodmoon Krew were already dug into Skarn's Maw when the Imperials arrived — survivors, it seems, of a crashed hulk centuries ago. The Orks are not leaving without a fight.

zones.name: Da Scrapyard
zones.description: A junk-moon of fused wreckage and scavenged plating, where Skarn's Maw's Orks drag anything that isn't nailed down. Half of it is stolen Imperial hardware; the other half used to be enemies.

log.text: Grots swarm the Scrapyard day and night, dragging in debris from the Rustfields to feed the Krew's ever-growing pile of 'good stuff.'

zones.name: Grimjaw's Roost
zones.description: Warboss Skarnag Grimjaw's personal stronghold, a fortress hacked together from three different crashed voidcraft. The biggest gun on the moon points outward. It has never needed to point inward.

log.text: Grimjaw declares himself 'Warboss of da whole Drift' from atop his Roost. Nobody has yet been foolish enough to tell him otherwise to his face.

zones.name: Necropolis
zones.description: A silent, glassy world long assumed dead. It was never dead — only sleeping. Its tomb complexes have begun to stir.

log.text: Auger scans of the tomb-world designated 'Necropolis' show no active signatures — for now. Astropaths report unquiet dreams when the fleet passes too close in the warp.

The unquiet dreams were a warning. Three tomb complexes beneath Necropolis's surface have opened. Reanimation protocols long dormant now flicker to life world-wide, and the world's ancient dynasty stirs to reclaim what was always theirs.

zones.name: The Silent Tomb
zones.description: A secondary tomb-complex linked to Necropolis by ancient subterranean causeways. Its cryptek engines began humming the same hour Necropolis's did — a dynasty waking in unison.

log.text: As Necropolis stirs, the Silent Tomb answers in kind. Canoptek scarabs pour from newly-opened seals, sweeping the surface clean of three centuries of dust — and anything else that happens to be there.

zones.name: The Silent Choir
zones.description: A stretch of void that used to hum with a mystery. Now it hums under Necron control, its resonance folded back into Necropolis's own network — exactly where the dynasty always intended it to end up.

log.text: Astropaths aboard three separate vessels reported the same dream on the same night: a choir singing in a language that predates the Imperium, emanating from an empty stretch of void. Navigators refuse to chart a course through it. Nobody has explained why the nebula there pulses, faintly, like a heartbeat.

Eldar farseers finally name what's been singing in the dark: not a ghost, not a nebula — a Necron resonance-ward, ancient even by Necropolis's standards, and it just synchronized with the tomb-world's own reactivation. Four separate Eldar forces move to seize or silence it before the dynasty can finish networking it in.

The Bonewrought Ward's defenses hold long enough for a second Necron phalanx to flank through the Choir's own resonance field, using the ward-signal itself as a targeting beacon. The dynasty's crypteks are reportedly delighted by the irony. The Silent Choir answers to Necropolis again.

zones.name: Ashen Reach
zones.description: A wasteland world scoured by ash storms, its skies now stained the color of old bone since the splinter fleet's arrival.

log.text: Imperial scouts report bio-signatures across Ashen Reach consistent with hive fleet spore contamination. No splinter fleet has been sighted yet — but the wind carries spores that shouldn't exist.

The spores were only the vanguard. A splinter fleet has translated in-system, and Ashen Reach's skies have gone the color of old bone. Bio-ships descend through the ash clouds, and the world's silence has become something far worse — hunger.

zones.name: The Gorge
zones.description: What used to be a moon is now barely recognizable — biomass sheeting over rock, the whole satellite slowly digesting itself into something the hive fleet can use.

log.text: The Gorge was a bare, unremarkable moon three days ago. It is unrecognizable now, its surface sheeted in pulsing biomass. Imperial auspex crews refuse to get close enough to confirm what's happening beneath.

zones.name: Spore Drift
zones.description: A slow-moving cloud of bio-spores drifting outward from Ashen Reach, thickening by the day. Anything that flies through it doesn't come out quite the same.

log.text: Long-range scans show the spore cloud has taken on a defined shape and a deliberate drift — as if something out there is steering it.

zones.name: The Gallowspire
zones.description: A once-Imperial listening post, its aquila replaced by something that shifts when stared at too long. Those who linger nearby report hearing their own voice calling from inside the rock.

log.text: Vox-logs recovered from a passing merchant vessel speak of a spire that should not still be standing — its Imperial aquila replaced by something that writhes when looked at too long. Those who venture too close report hearing their own voices, calling from inside the rock.

zones.name: Hate's Landing
zones.description: A blasted landing strip at the Gallowspire's foot, marked by a growing field of crude iconography scratched into the rock by hands that were, until recently, gauntleted in Imperial blue.

log.text: Traitor Marines make planetfall at what they've taken to calling Hate's Landing, raising banners that were burned — or so Imperial record insisted — over four hundred years ago.

zones.name: The Obsidian Skein
zones.description: A hidden webway port that opened in the shadow of a dead moon without warning. A kabal with old business in this system has returned to collect.

log.text: No astropath detected their arrival. No augur flagged their ships. The Obsidian Skein simply appeared one night in the shadow of a dead moon — a webway port opened by a kabal with old business in this system, and a taste for what the reopened Drift has to offer.

zones.name: The Bleeding Reach
zones.description: A raiding outpost bled into being at the Kabal's convenience — void-locks, torture-decks, and a launch bay for skiffs that never seem to return empty.

log.text: The Bleeding Reach comes online within hours of the Skein's arrival, its raiding skiffs already fanning out toward every unguarded world in the Drift.

zones.name: The Hollow Court
zones.description: A processing station where captives taken across the Drift are sorted, catalogued, and priced. The Archon holding court here is said to enjoy long negotiations more than short ones.

log.text: The Hollow Court opens for its first 'auction' since making planetfall in the Drift. Buyers are, discreetly, already arriving from three other factions.

zones.name: Ynnead's Veil
zones.description: A webway node that, by every Imperial record, should not exist. Craftworld seers walk here on business they share with no one.

log.text: The Craftworld seers arrived without warning and without fleet — stepping instead from a webway gate that, by every Imperial record, should not exist. They speak to no one of their purpose here, only that the threads of fate have drawn tight around the Drift, and they do not intend to be caught unprepared.

zones.name: The Last Grove
zones.description: A fragment of maiden-world greenery impossibly preserved inside a bubble of stabilized webway-space — a garden that should have died millennia ago, tended by someone, or something, still.

log.text: Seers pass through the Last Grove in silence, leaving small offerings among trees that, by any reasonable accounting, have no business still being alive.

zones.name: Sha'vastra Reach
zones.description: A T'au colonial foothold, its terraforming engines already running before the ash from the last warp storm had even settled. The Greater Good does not wait for permission.

log.text: Ethereal caste emissaries broadcast an open invitation on all frequencies: join the Greater Good, or step aside. The T'au colony ships arrived with terraforming engines already running, utterly undeterred by a system still smoldering from a warp storm's wake.

zones.name: Fio's Anchor
zones.description: A prefabricated construction platform dropped in-system ahead of the main colony fleet, already assembling the first ring of habitation modules. Efficient, orderly, and entirely uninvited by anyone already living in the Drift.

log.text: Fio caste engineers complete Fio's Anchor in under 30 hours — a construction speed that has made more than one Imperial officer deeply uneasy.

zones.name: Drift Station
zones.description: A derelict waystation sitting at the literal crossroads of the system. Whoever holds it controls the routes between every other world in the Drift — which is exactly why nobody does, for long.

log.text: Once a thriving waystation on the old trade route, the Drift Station now sits empty and unclaimed at the crossroads of the whole system — and every faction knows whoever holds it controls the routes between worlds.

Five warbands converge without warning: Drukhari raiders, an Astra Militarum column, an Ork Krew, a Necron honor guard, and a Tyranid bio-ship's opening wave. See the Campaign Log for the full account.

The dust settles at Drift Station, and it's Kabalite banners flying over the wreckage. The Astra Militarum column broke first, the Ork Krew's charge dissolved into a rout, the Necron honor guard was driven back beneath the station's foundations before it could fully deploy, and the Tyranid vanguard's opening wave died screaming in the void before the rest of the brood could translate in-system. The Obsidian Skein claims the crossroads — and with it, every route through the Drift.

zones.name: The Rustfields
zones.description: A thousand-kilometer debris field from a battle no living record explains. Salvage crews go in. Not all of them come back.

log.text: A debris field of shattered hulls stretches for a thousand kilometers, wreckage from a battle no living record accounts for. Salvage crews who venture in rarely come back with more than they went in with — and some don't come back at all.

zones.name: Ghoul Reef
zones.description: A mineral-rich asteroid belt that just became a great deal more interesting. Whatever the Cindergate was, it's Adeptus Mechanicus property now — and the Techpriests overseeing its excavation aren't taking questions.

log.text: Named for the ghostly static that plagues every vox-channel nearby, Ghoul Reef's asteroid belt is rich in rare minerals and, according to salvagers, richer still in bad luck. Three prospecting crews have vanished here since the Drift reopened.

The dead static that gave Ghoul Reef its name changes pitch for the first time anyone can remember — a rhythmic pulse bleeding out from somewhere deep in the asteroid field. Whatever is down there has been quiet for a very long time. It isn't anymore.

The dust settles, and it's a Mechanicus banner planted over what's left of the Cindergate. Eldar and Drukhari tore into each other before either could reach the structure, the Gallowspire's warband got caught in the crossfire, and the Tyranid broodswarm arrived just in time to feed on the wreckage of all three. The Techpriest expedition walked in when it mattered and walked out with whatever the Cindergate was hiding.

zones.name: Solthane Bastion
zones.description: A fortress-world the Astra Militarum raised in haste — and lost just as fast. Skarnag Grimjaw's warband walks its ramparts now, repainting the gun emplacements green and using the wreckage of the old garrison as a very large, very morbid trophy pile.

log.text: Engineering corps break ground on Solthane Bastion within a day of the order arriving from Kharvos Prime. High Command wants a fortified line to the north before anything currently out there decides to come looking.

Solthane Bastion falls hard and fast. Skarnag Grimjaw's Krew hits the line before the garrison can properly muster a response, and the fortress-world's own guns are turned inward within the hour. What's left of the human defense doesn't survive long enough to fall back.

zones.name: Highwatch Priory
zones.description: What the Space Marine liaison force didn't burn on their way out, the swarm has already started digesting. The watch-post's augur arrays still turn, uselessly, tracking nothing anyone alive still cares about.

log.text: Militarum engineers finish fortifying Highwatch within a day of Solthane's groundbreaking — and a Space Marine liaison force arrives not long after, here to see the line holds, not to hold it themselves.

The Space Marine liaison force at Highwatch reads the field correctly and pulls back in good order rather than be caught between an emboldened Ork Krew and the Tyranid vanguard grinding down from Voidmaw Rift. It's the right call — within a day, the swarm and the Orks are tearing into each other over the abandoned priory, and the swarm wins that particular argument.

zones.name: The Sanctum Vigil
zones.description: A shrine-fort overrun in the same push that broke Solthane Bastion. The Sisters' chapel still stands, technically — the Orks just don't see the point in knocking down something that useful as a mess hall.

log.text: The Sanctum Vigil is garrisoned by Militarum troops within the week, though it's the Sisters' benediction — delivered before their chaplaincy moved on to reinforce elsewhere — that the soldiers here credit for keeping the line quiet so far.
With Solthane broken, the Sanctum Vigil goes next — the same Ork warband riding the momentum straight through its gates. Whatever the Sisters' chaplaincy managed to evacuate, it wasn't much.

zones.name: Voidmaw Rift
zones.description: A tear in the system's northern dark where a second hive fleet splinter translated insystem, distinct from the one gorging itself on Ashen Reach. Bio-ships spawn from the Rift in ones and twos, probing south toward Solthane's lights.

log.text: Auspex stations at Solthane Bastion pick up bio-signatures translating in-system from the north — a second splinter fleet, unrelated to the one consuming Ashen Reach in the east. Voidmaw Rift is the name given to wherever it just tore its way into real space.

zones.name: The Chittering Waste
zones.description: A rocky moon overrun within hours of the splinter fleet's arrival, its surface now a carpet of feeder organisms clearing the ground for whatever comes next.

log.text: The Chittering Waste falls silent — and then anything but. Vox intercepts describe a sound like insects the size of hab-blocks, moving in the dark just past Highwatch’s sensor range.

zones.name: Bone-Ash Expanse
zones.description: A stripped, ash-grey world picked clean with unnatural speed, its surface littered with the calcified husks of whatever biomass the swarm didn't need. A warning, if anyone north of Solthane is still around to read it.

log.text: Long-range picts of the Bone-Ash Expanse show a world already stripped to the bone in less than a day. Militarum tacticians at Solthane revise their timeline for how long the Bastion has before contact.

zones.name: Grimfang Landing
zones.description: A crude but effective beachhead Skarnag Grimjaw's kin hammered together within sight of the Imperium's new bastion line — proof that no matter how fast the Munitorum builds a wall, there's always an Ork already looking at it funny.

log.text: Grimfang Landing goes up almost overnight, a scrapheap fortress planted defiantly close to the Sanctum Vigil's void-shields. Nobody sent these Orks an invitation to the fight brewing over the northern marches. They came anyway.

zones.name: Skullgrin Camp
zones.description: A forward raiding camp close enough to Bone-Ash Expanse that the Orks here can watch the Tyranid feeder-swarms at work through a scope — mostly, by all accounts, so they can time their raids for maximum chaos.

log.text: Skullgrin's boyz have taken to lobbing crude ordnance at anything that crawls out of Bone-Ash Expanse, less out of strategy than boredom. It's working better than it has any right to.

zones.name: The Bonewrought Ward
zones.description: A half-buried ward-spire on Necropolis's southern approach, silent for sixty million years until the dynasty's reawakening gave it a reason to open its eyes again. It exists for exactly one purpose: making sure nothing reaches the tomb-world uninvited.

log.text: The Bonewrought Ward’s weapon batteries cycle up for the first time in longer than the Imperium has existed. Necron sentries have clearly been briefed on what’s approaching from the direction of Ynnead’s Veil, and they are not interested in a diplomatic solution.
The Ward held. It was never really in doubt — sixty million years of patience doesn't break because four warhosts showed up on the same day.

zones.name: Aelindra's Waystone
zones.description: What's left of an Eldar forward waystone, its wraithbone lattice stripped for parts by the same Necron force that turned the Choir's own signal into a targeting beacon against it.

log.text: Four separate Eldar warhosts converge on the newly-raised waystone within a day of each other — an unusually large commitment for a single objective, which tells its own story about how seriously the farseers are taking whatever the Choir turns out to be.

By the time the Eldar realized the Choir wasn't the objective but the weapon, Aelindra's Waystone was already being dismantled. Whatever four warhosts' worth of coordination was supposed to look like, it didn't survive contact with either the enemy or each other.

eventLog.text:
THE BATTLE FOR DRIFT STATION — Five banners converge on the system's crossroads.

Word of Drift Station's emptiness has spread fast — too fast. A Kabal of the Obsidian Skein slips from the webway in raiding skiffs, hungry for slaves and sport. An Astra Militarum relief column from Kharvos Prime arrives to secure the waystation before it falls to xenos hands. Skarnag Grimjaw's Bloodmoon Krew roars in from Skarn's Maw, drawn by nothing more than the promise of a good scrap. Beneath the station's ancient foundations, Necron warriors phase into being — Necropolis's dynasty does not tolerate trespassers on ground it once called its own. And in the ash-choked void above, a Tyranid bio-ship vents its first wave of gaunts toward the drifting hulk, drawn by the sheer press of biomass converging below.

Five factions. One station. No alliances, no truce — only the Drift, and whoever's left standing when the void goes quiet again.

STORM ON THE NORTHERN MARCHES

While the dust hasn't yet settled over Drift Station, vox-traffic from the system's northern dark tells a second story. The Astra Militarum has broken ground on Solthane Bastion, extending the line to Highwatch and the Sanctum Vigil alongside it — Munitorum banners over all three. Allies have answered the muster in support rather than command: a Space Marine liaison force at Highwatch, and an Adepta Sororitas chaplaincy lending its blessing at the Vigil before moving on.

They have good reason to hurry. A second hive fleet splinter — unconnected to the one devouring Ashen Reach — has torn into real space at Voidmaw Rift, and it is not waiting politely. The Chittering Waste and the Bone-Ash Expanse have already fallen, stripped in less than a day.

And, inevitably, the noise has drawn other eyes. Ork raiders out of Skarn's Maw haven't just been probing the frontier — they've planted a flag. Grimfang Landing and the Skullgrin Camp have gone up within sight of both the Sanctum Vigil and Bone-Ash Expanse, an Ork foothold wedged directly between two much larger wars. Three banners are converging on the northern marches, and for the first time, all three are close enough to see each other.

THE OBSIDIAN SKEIN TAKES THE CROSSROADS

Five banners went into Drift Station. One came out standing. The Astra Militarum relief column broke and fell back toward Kharvos Prime, the Bloodmoon Krew's charge dissolved into a rout, a Necron honor guard was driven back beneath the station's foundations before it could fully deploy, and the Tyranid vanguard's opening wave was cut down before the rest of the bio-ship's brood could translate in-system. When the void went quiet, it was Kabalite blades doing the counting.

Drift Station now flies the Obsidian Skein's colors — and with the crossroads in Drukhari hands, every route through the Kharvos Drift runs through territory they control. The other four factions have a great deal to say about that. None of it complimentary.

THE FALL OF THE NORTHERN LINE

The defense of Solthane Bastion doesn't hold. Skarnag Grimjaw's Krew breaks through before the garrison can properly answer, and Astra Militarum command overseeing the line falls in the opening hours of the assault. The Sanctum Vigil goes next, taken in the same push. Only the Space Marine liaison force at Highwatch reads the field in time — pulling back rather than standing to be ground up between an emboldened Ork warband and the Tyranid vanguard already pressing down from Voidmaw Rift.

Without an Imperial line left to break, the two invaders turn on each other over what remains. Highwatch changes hands one more time before the fighting settles: the swarm wins that argument, consuming the abandoned priory in short order. The Orks, already dug in at Solthane and the Vigil, don't contest it further — there's still plenty to hold, and holding it is more an Ork specialty than pushing further into a hungry tree line.

The northern marches are lost. Astra Militarum command will have questions about how quickly. The Space Marines, at least, live to answer them.

THE CINDERGATE SIGNAL

While the northern marches burn, the Adeptus Mechanicus decides — with characteristic priorities — that it isn't their war. Aurun's Forge quietly diverts a second expedition, not north to reinforce Solthane's ashes, but south toward Ghoul Reef, where auspex arrays have picked up a structure buried deep in the asteroid field: something old, something that shouldn't still have power, and something that just started broadcasting.

The Mechanicus isn't alone in noticing. A Kabal out of the Obsidian Skein — never one to let anyone else profit from a good mystery unattended — burns hard for the Reef. Eldar seers at Ynnead's Veil, who have spent this whole campaign speaking of threads drawing tight, finally say the quiet part aloud: whatever is in that rock matters, and they intend to reach it first, or make sure no one else keeps it. A warband breaks from the Gallowspire, drawn by something in the signal that speaks a language older than the Emperor's Imperium. And in the ash-dark beyond it all, a bio-ship changes course — the Hive Mind has felt the pulse too, and it does not ignore things that think.

Five banners, one buried secret, and a Techpriest expedition that would very much like everyone else to leave before they have to explain the paperwork. The Cindergate, whatever it is, is about to have visitors.

THE MECHANICUS CLAIMS THE CINDERGATE

Five banners came for the Cindergate. The Adeptus Mechanicus barely had to fight for it.

Eldar and Drukhari clashed first — old grudges reasserting themselves the moment both fleets arrived, neither willing to let the other near the signal first. The Gallowspire's warband tried to exploit the opening and got caught between both xenos forces for its trouble. And when the Tyranid broodswarm finally arrived, it found four exhausted, bleeding forces instead of one — and simply started feeding on whichever was closest.

While the Reef burned around them, the Techpriest expedition did what the Mechanicus does best: it waited, catalogued, and moved only when the calculus favored certainty over glory. By the time the other factions had ground each other down, servitor crews had already breached the Cindergate's outer shell — and whatever ancient systems still lived inside it apparently recognized something in the Mechanicus's approach, because it let them in without a fight. The other four factions got the opposite welcome on their way out.

Ghoul Reef now flies the Cog Mechanicus's banner, and Aurun's Forge has a great deal of new data to process. The Mechanicus is not, by all reports, in any hurry to share what it found.

ECHOES OF THE WAR IN HEAVEN

Long before there was an Imperium, before there was a Drift to fight over, there was a war between the Necrontyr and the Aeldari empire that predates every banner currently flying over the Kharvos system. Nobody currently drawing breath here remembers it. The Silent Choir, it turns out, does.

Eldar farseers have finally identified the source of the void's endless, wordless hum: a Necron resonance-ward, buried and dormant for sixty million years, that just changed its frequency in perfect synchrony with Necropolis's own reawakening. That is, by any reading, a very bad sign — and the Aeldari response is not subtle. Four separate warhosts have committed to the Choir's seizure, converging from Ynnead's Veil and a newly-raised waystone planted defiantly on the tomb-world's own doorstep.

The dynasty's answer is exactly what sixty million years of patience would suggest: the Bonewrought Ward, an outer defense spire nobody knew was still capable of opening its eyes, has woken up specifically to make sure it doesn't have to ask twice. Two Necron forces now stand against four Aeldari warhosts, refighting — on a much smaller scale — a war that ended before either side's current soldiers were anything but potential.

THE CHOIR FALLS SILENT ONCE MORE

Two Necron forces against four Aeldari warhosts should not have been close. It wasn't — just not in the direction the Eldar expected.

Whatever coordination existed between the four warhosts converging on Aelindra's Waystone evidently didn't survive first contact with each other's battle-plans, let alone the enemy's. The Bonewrought Ward's reawakened defenses held the line long enough for a second phalanx to flank around through the Choir's own resonance field — using the ward-signal itself as a targeting beacon, an irony the dynasty's crypteks were reportedly delighted by. By the time the Eldar realized the ward wasn't the objective but the weapon, Aelindra's Waystone was already being dismantled for parts.

The Silent Choir belongs to Necropolis again, and it isn't singing to anyone else's frequency now. Whatever the Eldar farseers foresaw when they committed four warhosts to this fight, it evidently wasn't this.
